Code Summary: This repository provides a Nextflow workflow pipeline for systematically identifying and analyzing "dark" and "camouflaged" genomic regions that cannot be adequately assembled or aligned using standard short-read sequencing technologies. The pipeline consists of two main workflows: one to identify and mask dark/camouflaged regions for a given genome version, and another to rescue variants from these camouflaged regions in sequencing datasets, enabling researchers to call mutations that would otherwise be completely overlooked by standard variant callers.

Biomedical Relevance: YES. This repository is biomedically relevant as it provides a DNA methylation biomarker tool for measuring the pace of biological aging. While not exclusively focused on neurodegenerative diseases, biological aging is a fundamental risk factor for age-related conditions including neurological disorders like Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease. The tool analyzes epigenetic biomarkers from blood samples to assess aging-related health outcomes, disease risk, disability, and mortality, making it relevant to biomedical research on aging and age-related diseases.
Code Summary: DunedinPACE is an R package that calculates a DNA methylation-based biomarker measuring the pace of biological aging from blood samples. The package takes DNA methylation beta values from Illumina arrays (450k, EPIC, or EPICv2) as input and outputs DunedinPACE values that quantify how fast or slow an individual is aging relative to the normative rate of one year per calendar year. The tool was developed using longitudinal data from the Dunedin Study tracking 19 biomarkers of organ system integrity over 20 years.

Tooling: - R programming language - devtools (for package installation) - Illumina methylation arrays (450k, EPIC, EPICv2 platforms) - DNA methylation beta value matrices - GitHub for code distribution
